page.layout: Full-width heading at the top, centred (dedicatory superscription). Below it one column of italic verse, with a woodcut initial at the start. Catchword at the lower right. No margin text.

l.i: F[?]oetus ut eximia est proprij nota saepè
parentis,
Ac utriusq; uno corpore dona gerit:
Sic Cuculus Smidline tuus, quem nuper Achate
Holdero adideras, quis sit utrq; docet.
Insignis certè proles, dignissima patre,
Et quàm perpetua posteritate bees:
Sic Bibenhusiaco semper laudaberis antro,
Egregiaq; quòd sis progenerator avis:
Vt quæ caeruleis te, scilicet, intulit astris,
In terrisq; almum nomen habere dedit.
Namq; timore suo, simul atq; referre timorem
Ipsa tuum poterit, quem perhibere soles,
Non quæ casta Dei mens approbat omnipotētis.
Ast quæ & crudelis Rex Phlegetontis habet.
Dogmata cœlestis fugis illustrissima Iovæ
Necnon & seruos, organa sancta, Dei,
Quos fore crediderás semper, qui pellere possent
Coccysmos, recta quos sine mente canis.
Sic, ut & astutus Cuculus, tu ornare palumbem
Infamem cogitas calliditate tua:

page.notes: The woodcut initial is a decorated E-shaped letter. I read it as F (Foetus), but this is uncertain, so the letter is marked [?]. The word after the initial is printed "Oetus"; the initial is treated as its first letter. Doubtful readings: "Cuculus" (the second u is printed unusually), "bees" (possibly "beas" or "beës"), "Iovæ" (printed as Iova/Iouæ), "crediderás" (accent uncertain), "quæ" (ligature). The verse lines are joined into one paragraph because the poem is one stanza without printed breaks. No page number or running head is printed. The top margin shows show-through from the reverse, which is not transcribed.
